narrative: You are currently seeking a loan of 3,394 DM to fund home repairs, a request that comes at a time when you are managing your household as a 65-year-old without current employment. Based on an analysis of your financial profile, there is a 58% probability that this credit arrangement would represent a high risk for the bank, which has unfortunately led to the denial of your application. The most significant factor in this decision is the current status of your checking account, which shows a negative balance. This is a notable concern because, while nearly half of approved applicants have no debt in their checking accounts, only about 20% of successful borrowers share your current status of being below zero. Furthermore, your requested repayment period of 42 months is more than double the 19-month average seen in successful applications, creating a long-term financial commitment that the model flags as a significant risk. Such a lengthy duration increases the uncertainty of repayment, especially when compared to the shorter terms typically granted to others in similar situations. Interestingly, your credit history—specifically your experience with other existing credits—actually worked in your favor by demonstrating a long-term engagement with the banking system. This history helped lower your risk profile slightly, as it suggests you are a known borrower, which the model views more favorably than someone with no credit history at all. However, this positive factor was not enough to outweigh the immediate concerns regarding your current liquidity and the length of the loan. Your situation is further influenced by your current lack of steady employment, which makes a long-term debt of this size more difficult to sustain over several years. To improve your chances for a future application, we recommend focusing on maintaining a positive balance in your checking account for several consecutive months to demonstrate stability. You might also consider requesting a smaller loan amount or a significantly shorter repayment duration, which would align more closely with the profiles of typically approved borrowers. Strengthening your savings beyond the current level of less than 100 DM would also provide a more robust financial cushion that could change the outcome of a future review. Taking these steps to show a period of financial consistency will be key to demonstrating that you can comfortably manage new installments.
